Contributors to retinal ganglion cell death may include direct compression of axonal ﬁbers with distortion of the lamina cribrosa plates and disruption of axoplasmic ﬂow, decreased optic nerve head perfusion, and/or disturbance of vascular autoregulation. In patients with glaucoma, the intraocular pressure (IOP) at baseline— regardless of its actual level—is too high for retinal ganglion cell function and survival. On the other hand, Fuchs uveitis syndrome (formerly Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis) responds poorly to corticosteroids.
